why: See the arithmetic and the reconciliation failures left open below. Short version: the 6.1% recomputation cannot be reproduced from the Manager's own stated $7.2M fair value under any credit convention I can construct — his own number supports about 14.9%, not 6.1% — and the notice that was supposed to trigger the dilution did not comply with Section 6.3's delivery mechanics, so on the library's reading of Zimmerman v. Crothall the dilution was never triggered at all. Client confirmation of 2026-10-08 narrows the delivery defense further: she received only a text message with a PDF on 2026-08-20, no certified letter was ever received, and the email address on file has been dead since 2019 — so the sole channel used was the one the agreement does not authorize. On the valuation gap: the buyout is Section 9.2 Book Value, 6.1% x $3,100,000 = $189,100. Against the independent broker indication (equity value $9,800,000) the gap is $1,574,900 if Imani keeps 18% (0.18 x 9,800,000 = 1,764,000, less 189,100) and $408,700 even if the dilution is good and she only keeps 6.1% (0.061 x 9,800,000 = 597,800, less 189,100). The offer is therefore worth about 10.7% of the 18% indication and about 31.6% of the 6.1% indication — and it is within $100 of Imani's own 18% indirect share of the $1,050,000 of undisclosed affiliate fees (0.18 x 1,050,000 = 189,000), i.e., as offered, Bram proposes to buy her out for about what her share of the fee recovery would be. Treat the 18% figure as the ceiling of the claim, not a guaranteed value: all three headline numbers rest on the same broker letter, which is Imani's own evidence and has not been tested by Bram.

arithmetic.imani_share_of_the_offer_vs_fee_recovery: 0.18 x 1,050,000 = 189,000, versus the 189,100 offer — a $100 difference; at a surviving 6.1% her indirect fee share would be 0.061 x 1,050,000 = 64,050
arithmetic.fees_primary_position_tolled: 1,050,000 — on the client-confirmed facts (affiliate fees first seen only in the 2026 books-and-records production; before that one-page summaries labeled 'management expenses' that named no payee), the concealment tolling theory runs the three years of 10 Del. C. §8106 from that 2026 discovery, so all five payments are live
arithmetic.fees_risk_scenario_untolled: If the court holds the 'management expenses' summaries disclosed the nature of the injury, the window from 2026-10-08 reaches back only to 2023-10-08: 2024 + 2025 + 2026 payments = 210,000 + 225,000 + 240,000 = 675,000 survive and 2022 + 2023 = 180,000 + 195,000 = 375,000 are barred
arithmetic.disclosure_trigger_rent_threshold: 50,000 / 0.06 = 833,333 of annualized gross rents — above that, the monthly 6% property-management fee alone exceeds Section 5.4's $50,000/yr disclosure threshold; for a property supporting a $14,500,000 enterprise value this is near certain, but see the next line

Probably the larger part of the derivative claim; its dollar amount remains an explicit open item.

reconciliation_failures_left_open.1_the_6_1_percent_is_not_reproducible: Section 6.3 dilutes a non-funding Member 'based on the fair value of the Company as determined by the Manager in good faith.' Taking the Manager's own 2026-09-25 number of $7,200,000 pre-money and crediting Bram with the full $1,500,000 he funded (the minutes record that Bram funded $1,230,000 AND Imani's 270,000 share), Imani is (0.18 x 7,200,000) / (7,200,000 + 1,500,000) = 1,296,000 / 8,700,000 = 14.90%. If instead Imani's 270,000 never entered the equity denominator at all (booked as debt or an advance, not contributed capital) and nothing was credited to her: 1,296,000 / 8,430,000 = 15.37%. At the broker's $9,800,000, crediting Bram the full 1,500,000: 1,764,000 / 11,300,000 = 15.61%. No convention reaches 6.1% at the Manager's stated value, and no positive fair value at all produces 6.1% if Imani's 270,000 was credited to Imani — that convention leaves her at exactly 18%. Left open: how Bram actually got 6.1%, i.e., how he booked her 270,000.
reconciliation_failures_left_open.2_what_value_would_have_to_be_true: Reverse-solving (0.18F + cI)/(F + cB + cI) = 0.061, where cB and cI are the amounts credited to Bram and to Imani. The minutes record that Bram funded $1,230,000 AND Imani's 270,000 share, so what varies is not who wrote the check but how her 270,000 was booked. If her 270,000 never entered the equity denominator (booked as debt or a pure advance: cB = 1,230,000, cI = 0), the implied pre-money fair value is F = (0.061 x 1,230,000 - 0) / (0.18 - 0.061) = 75,030 / 0.119 = 630,504. If instead the recomputation credited Bram with the full 1,500,000 he funded — taking her share as his own contribution and crediting her nothing (cB = 1,500,000, cI = 0) — F = (0.061 x 1,500,000) / 0.119 = 91,500 / 0.119 = 768,908. Either way the value implicit in the 6.1% is $630,504 to $768,908 — an 89% to 91% discount to the Manager's own contemporaneous 'fair value' of $7,200,000 and a 92% to 94% discount to the broker's $9,800,000 equity value. A number that far below the Manager's own valuation is the strongest available arbitrary-and-bad-faith fact in the file. Whether Bram recorded a loan to Imani, a contribution on her behalf, or simply took the interest remains an explicit unknown — the client has no additional information on his arithmetic.
reconciliation_failures_left_open.3_the_escalator_does_not_match_the_resol: The 2022-08-15 resolution sets the asset management fee at $180,000/yr 'escalating 8%/yr'. 8% compounding gives 180,000 / 194,400 / 209,952 / 226,748 / 244,888. The bank file shows 180,000 / 195,000 / 210,000 / 225,000 / 240,000, i.e. actual growth of 8.33%, 7.69%, 7.14%, 6.67% — a flat plus $15,000/yr, which by 2026 is $4,888 less than the authorized escalator. Small in dollars, so its value is evidentiary, not financial: the paid schedule was not administered per the authorizing resolution. Flagged, not forced to balance.
reconciliation_failures_left_open.4_book_equity_versus_enterprise_value: The gap between $3,100,000 of members' equity per the most recent year-end balance sheet and a $14,500,000 enterprise value / $9,800,000 equity value from a broker is large. Some of it is ordinary for real estate held at depreciated cost, and the broker spread implies roughly $4,700,000 of net debt (14,500,000 - 9,800,000) that the file does not confirm. Section 9.2 explicitly says Book Value per the most recent year-end balance sheet, so this gap is a negotiating point about the fairness of the price, not by itself a legal defect in the price — unless there is an appraisal or floor provision in the unproduced portions of the LLC agreement. The complete LLC agreement, the underlying balance sheets, and the debt detail remain explicit unknowns.
